title: navigation: read a nav entry's declared API `dataSource`, so its `visible` sees the selected value as `data` (the objectui renderer half of objectstack-ai/objectstack#24427)
body:
Filed by the triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015, `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U`). The maintainer agreed in chat on 2026-10-19 (「同意你的建议」) to the seat's lean on the 18.0 GA scope: "the backend ships as it is; file an objectui card for 18.1". ⛔ Not a claim.

Blocked-by: #12971

**Filing gate ③.** This is a follow-up that a landed spec card names. The spec half, objectstack-ai/objectstack#24427 (`26501ae24f`, Part of objectstack-ai/objectstack#24332), says in its own docblock (`packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts:410`–`:417` on objectstack `origin/main` `fb9c22aa09`): "The reader is the objectui renderer half, filed when this lands." No objectui card was filed. A search of this repository's issues (open and closed) for titles with nav × dataSource / data source found none.

## What the spec now allows

- `BaseNavItemSchema.dataSource` is `ElementApiDataSourceSchema.optional()`, the page element's API binding by reference: `{ provider: 'api', read: { url }, path? }`.
  - It is carried by all nine branches that spread the base: `object`, `dashboard`, `page`, `url`, `report`, `action`, `component`, `doc` and `group`.
- Only `visible` reads the bound value, as `data` (e.g. `data.total == 1`).
  - `label` and the target keys take no `data`.
  - The binding is not published to `children`.
- The key is described `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]`.
  - Its liveness row is `packages/spec/liveness/app.json` → `navigation.children.dataSource`, `planned`, with an author warning.
  - The marker leaves the describe, and the row flips to `live`, when this card ships.

## What objectui does today (`origin/main` `4484a11041`)

- `packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx:682` (`passesNavItemGuards`) evaluates `item.visible` against the shell's ambient scope, which has no `data` in it. The two other callers share that guard:
  - `packages/app-shell/src/chrome/CommandPalette.tsx:154`;
  - `packages/app-shell/src/views/nav-menu-renderer.tsx:324`.
- The page element's reader already exists: `useElementApiDataSource` in `packages/react/src/element-data-source/`, used by `SchemaRenderer`. Reuse it rather than writing a second fetch.

## Done when

1. A nav entry that declares `dataSource` is shown or hidden by its `visible` over the value the binding selects, in the sidebar, the command palette and the nav menu alike. They share one guard, so they cannot disagree.
2. An entry without `dataSource` behaves exactly as today.
3. A failed or pending read hides the entry rather than showing it (fail closed). This matches how the page element's binding treats an unanswered read. Pin it.
4. Objectstack follow-up: the `[PLANNED — not yet rendered]` marker leaves the describe, and the liveness row flips to `live`. That is one `domain:spec` change on objectstack after this card lands. Name it in the PR.

## Why p2 and not `target:v18`

- This is a widening reader, so it can land in any 18.x minor without breaking an application. The spec already tells authors the key is not rendered yet.
- objectstack-ai/objectstack#24332's ruling also left the named consumer, objectstack-ai/cloud#3002's sidebar row, free to drop that nav entry instead (「如果开发复杂的话，3002 也可以删除左侧的导航项」).

Dedupe words: navigation dataSource reader, nav visible data, NavigationRenderer passesNavItemGuards data scope, ElementApiDataSource nav entry, liveness navigation.children.dataSource planned.
